content:
Apple has put considerable effort into the Apple TV Remote app experience in iOS 27, which is also a clear signal that a new Apple TV 4K box is on the way.

It all starts with iOS 27 beta 1. Apple has restored the Remote app from its previous half-baked state as a Control Center widget back into a full app that can live on the home screen.

This change applies to iPhone and iPad. Apple Watch has long had its own dedicated Remote app. As for Mac, I happen to have just put together an app for that.

Looking ahead, "pdfu" on X has uncovered some interesting new features coming to the iOS Remote app. These new features aren't visible in the interface just yet, but are tucked away behind feature flags. This coding whiz managed to demonstrate how they work.

It looks set to be a major upgrade for the iPhone and iPad Remote app. The current version mainly acts as virtual direction buttons, essentially using software to mimic the physical remote. The new version goes further, making the most of what software can do.

Apple is also expected to update the physical Siri Remote alongside the launch of the new Apple TV 4K, hopefully within the next month or two.

All this activity around the software remote is a clear sign that Apple is paying more attention to the hardware box. Generally speaking, this means a new product is in the works.
